one_liner: Archived Intel fork of zlib with SSE4.2 hashing and new quick/medium deflate strategies; about 1.8x stock zlib at mid levels.
what_it_does: A source- and API-compatible fork of madler/zlib (HEAD reports ZLIB_VERSION 1.2.13 after a November 2022 re-apply of the patches) that writes standard zlib, gzip and raw deflate streams through the normal deflateInit/deflate/inflate/gz* API. Applications relink against it with no code changes. It was shipped for x86/x64 as 'zlib-intel' inside the .NET runtime's System.IO.Compression before .NET moved to zlib-ng.
how_it_is_fast: Deflate hashes 4 bytes with one SSE4.2 crc32 instruction (inline asm, chosen at runtime by a CPUID check) instead of zlib's rolling shift-xor hash, slides the hash table with SSE2, and uses 16-bit unaligned compares in longest_match. Levels 4-6 run deflate_medium, a match-extending strategy that avoids zlib's lazy evaluation, and the optional deflate_quick (level 1) compares with SSE4.2 pcmpestri, emits only static-Huffman blocks and caps the window at 8 KiB (windowBits 13). The gzip path folds CRC-32 with PCLMULQDQ while copying input (crc_fold_copy).
when_to_use: Reproducing or studying the 2014-era Intel deflate work that zlib-ng later merged (deflate_quick, deflate_medium, CRC hashing).
Legacy x86-64 builds already pinned to zlib-intel (for example older .NET runtimes) that need an audit trail of what they ship.

Mid-level (4-6) compression on x86 of text or executables where a zlib-1.2.13 API is required and zlib-ng's compat mode is not an option: Snellman's zlib-bench README shows level 5 at 52.8-56.1% of stock zlib time.
when_not_to_use: Any new project: Intel archived it on 2024-03-01 ('This project will no longer be maintained by Intel ... no longer accepts patches'), and zlib-ng carries the same quick and medium strategies with runtime dispatch, ARM support and active maintenance.

Correctness-critical pipelines: issue #24 'deflate_medium doesn't always produce output that can be inflated' (2019) is still open, as are inflate reports #21 (corrupted output on ~8-byte inputs after commit 62b7616), #33 (zip member inflated 6,906 bytes short, v1.2.11.1_jtkv6.3) and #34 (checksum failure with windowBits 47, reported by the .NET team); none has a maintainer reply, and whether the 2022 rebase fixed them is not documented.
Incompressible data such as JPEG: zlib-bench shows level 5 at 115.4% of baseline time, i.e. slower than stock zlib.

Non-x86 targets: Makefile.in and CMakeLists.txt compile crc_folding.c and deflate_quick.c with -mpclmul -msse4 unconditionally, and the x86 code paths are the whole point; use zlib-ng or stock zlib on ARM.
Security-sensitive deployments: it stops at zlib 1.2.13, so upstream fixes from zlib 1.3 onward are not merged.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (configure/make or CMake)
integration.min_toolchain: C89-style zlib 1.2.13 code base; GCC or Clang with -msse4/-mpclmul support (inline asm in deflate_quick needs GCC-style asm outside MSVC)
integration.platforms: x86-64 and x86-32 (SSE2 required for the build; SSE4.2 and PCLMULQDQ used when CPUID reports them); other architectures not supported by the build files
integration.thread_safety: Same as zlib for separate z_stream objects (bundled README: 'All the code is thread safe'), but x86_check_features() sets global feature flags behind an unsynchronised static once flag on every deflateInit, a benign but formal data race when streams are created concurrently.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same zlib 1.2.13 API, ABI and stream format, but x86-only, compressed bytes differ from stock zlib, and the fast level-1 strategy is not compiled in by default

gotchas: deflate_quick is off in current HEAD: it is wrapped in #ifdef USE_QUICK and nothing in configure, Makefile.in or CMakeLists.txt defines it, whereas the 2014 commit benchmarked by zlib-bench (e176b3c) added -DUSE_QUICK -DUSE_MEDIUM in configure. A default HEAD build therefore runs deflate_fast with the CRC hash at level 1, and the 2014 'level 1 at 36% of baseline time' result does not describe it; add -DUSE_QUICK to get it.
With USE_QUICK, level 1 silently reduces windowBits to 13 (8 KiB window), which is why its ratio drops (0.46 vs 0.37 of input size on the executable in the 2014 run).
The public crc32() function is stock zlib 1.2.13; the PCLMULQDQ folding is used only inside deflate's gzip wrapper path.

Past memory-safety fixes show the risk profile: out-of-bounds reads in crc_folding (issue #15) and fizzle_matches (#3), and 'deflate_medium: avoid out-of-bounds read' landed only in the November 2022 rebase.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Essentially never for new code: zlib-ng (catalogued, with lzbench numbers) contains these same Intel strategies plus ARM and AVX2/AVX-512 paths and is maintained; Cloudflare's fork is the comparable deprecated alternative and is faster at levels 6-9. Keep this entry for attribution and for auditing systems that still ship zlib-intel.
verified_claims_summary: Juho Snellman's independent zlib-bench harness (github.com/jsnell/zlib-bench) pins madler/zlib 5089329, cloudflare a80420c and Intel e176b3c and builds each with ./configure && make; its README example run at level 5 shows Intel at 1.49 s vs 2.66 s baseline on an executable (56.1%), 0.85 vs 1.62 s on HTML (52.8%) and 1.08 vs 0.93 s on JPEG (115.4%), with decompression at 97.6-103.2% of baseline. CPU and compiler are not stated in the repo; the blog's level-1 numbers and the i7-4770 came from search snippets only, and all of it measures the 2014 zlib 1.2.8-based state, not the 1.2.13 HEAD.
status_note: Abandoned: archived by Intel on 2024-03-01 with an explicit no-maintenance notice and several open correctness reports; Zlib-licensed so vendoring is legal, but zlib-ng is the maintained successor.
